audit_scope.description: Trust model for EIP-3540 (EOF Container Format), EIP-4881 (Deposit Tree Snapshots), EIP-7749 (Wallet Intended Validator Signing), EIP-7549 (Attestation Aggregation), and EIP-3085 (wallet_addEthereumChain). Covers EOF validation, CL deposit lifecycle, wallet RPC signing flows, attestation gossip, and chain addition security boundaries.

misclassified_entities.reason: Contract Caller represents an internal EVM call context (CALL/STATICCALL/DELEGATECALL), which is an internal EVM component, not an external entity
Malicious Actor is a threat actor description, not a legitimate external entity in the system architecture
Potentially Malicious Dapp is a threat-modeled variant of EXT-DAPP; the threat framing should be in the security analysis, not as a separate external entity
Signature Presenter in EIP-7749 validation subgraph represents an internal contract call submitting a signature for verification, which is an internal EVM interaction

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any EOA or contract can submit deployment transactions containing arbitrary bytecode. EOF validation must reject malformed containers regardless of deployer identity.

trusted_external_entities.name: Prospective Validator
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators submit deposit transactions to the EL deposit contract. The deposit contract validates signatures and amounts but the submitter is untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Chain Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers providing deposit tree snapshots could be malicious. Snapshot data must be validated by recalculating deposit root before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: Syncing Consensus Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Clients requesting deposit snapshots are unauthenticated HTTP callers. Rate limiting and input validation are required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Decentralized Application (EIP-7749)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: dApps requesting wallet signatures are untrusted. The wallet must display validator address and data to the user for explicit approval before signing.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Human users interact via wallet UI. While they approve actions, they may be phished or confused. The wallet should provide clear information but cannot trust user judgment.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Chain Validator
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Attestation creation and broadcast via CL
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Active validators have staked 32 ETH and are economically incentivized to behave correctly. However, they can still attempt gossip mutation attacks, so committee membership verification is required.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers can be malicious and may attempt gossip mutation attacks by modifying the committee index field. Pre-cache committee membership verification is required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Decentralized Application (EIP-3085)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: dApps requesting chain addition may be malicious, attempting to add fraudulent chain configurations with deceptive RPC endpoints. Chain ID verification against RPC endpoints and explicit user consent are required.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All submitted bytecode is treated as untrusted. EOF validation must reject containers with invalid magic bytes, section ordering, size violations, or stray bytes.
Deposit transactions are validated by the deposit contract for correct pubkey, withdrawal credentials, amount, and BLS signature.
Snapshot data must be validated by recalculating deposit root from finalized hashes before acceptance. Root mismatch indicates corrupted or malicious snapshot.
HTTP endpoint must handle unauthenticated requests safely. Snapshot generation should use consistent finalized state view.
Wallet must display validator address and data to user. EIP-191 prefix (0x19 || 0x00) ensures domain separation preventing cross-context signature reuse and transaction replay.
Committee membership must be verified before caching attestations. Gossip mutation attacks where peers modify the committee index must be detected and rejected.
Chain parameters are untrusted input. Chain ID must be verified against RPC endpoints. Only HTTPS URLs accepted. User must be warned about RPC exposure and must explicitly approve chain addition.

coverage_gaps: EXT-USER (wallet user) has no direct boundary edge to EL infrastructure; interaction is mediated through wallet UI
EXT-VALIDATOR-EIP7549 boundary is at the CL gossip layer, not directly at EL interfaces
